solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Silly act, with that woman's underwear in

parts.note: a feat is a deed or act
her is the possessive for that woman
a bra is an item of women's underwear

explanation.surface: A daft performance in which someone's lingerie is put on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly used as a noun, as in 'you silly', is a scatterbrained person, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Flip ace of suit out of sequence

indicators.note: cards out of sequence are disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A card player turns over the ace of a suit that was not in its proper order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flip' looks like turning a card over; it is the definition, meaning flippant.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip is informal for flippant, and flippant remarks are jokey and lacking seriousness.

clue.text: It's nearly All Fool's Day — get protective clothing

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: All Fools' Day is April 1, written as APR (the abbreviation for April) and ONE

explanation.surface: As April 1 approaches, someone is told to put on protective gear against pranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the final E of APR ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore worn over clothes to keep them clean in the kitchen or workshop is protective clothing.

clue.text: Back Italy's language

parts.note: hind means at the back, as in hind legs
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An instruction to support the Italian tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the principal official language of India, spoken across the north of the country.

clue.text: Cut wood supporting seats

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath the other one

parts.note: rumps are backsides, what one sits on
teak is a hardwood

explanation.surface: A carpenter trims the timber that holds up the chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut in butchery is a joint or piece of meat, and this one comes from the hindquarters of beef.

clue.text: Played red ace with ten, and played again

indicators.note: played in the sense of toyed with, so the letters are shuffled about

explanation.surface: A card game in which red ace and ten were laid down, and the hand was replayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Played' is the anagram signal; the second is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform a scene or event a second time is to act it out once more.

clue.text: Presses offices of tax and statistics

parts.note: IR is the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority
ONS is the Office for National Statistics, the UK statistics body

explanation.surface: Government departments for tax and figures are leaning on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the UK's tax office before merging into HMRC.
explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes is to smooth them with a hot iron, so both verbs mean flatten creases.

clue.text: Redress main cost with open payout

indicators.note: letters paid out are let loose and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Damages covering the main cost come with an open-ended settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress is a remedy for a wrong, typically money paid to make amends for loss.

clue.text: Happen to recall former police company

indicators.note: recall is read as calling back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: RUC is the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the former Northern Ireland police force

explanation.surface: Something brings to mind an old police unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was replaced by the Police Service of Northern Ireland in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean take place or come about as an event.

clue.text: Person taking more painkillers? That's me

parts.note: someone dosed with more painkillers is more numb, read as numb plus -er
one is a person, as in 'one should'

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being the one who swallows extra analgesics.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word is read not as 'quantity' but as 'more numb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking after number one means looking after oneself, so the phrase stands for the speaker.

clue.text: Fit place for people doing stretches?

definitions.text: Fit place for people doing stretches?

parts.words: Fit place for people doing stretches?
parts.note: a stretch is slang for a prison sentence, and fit means suitable as well as healthy

explanation.surface: A gym or studio suited to people limbering up.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners serving sentences take their outdoor exercise in an enclosed courtyard of the jail.

clue.text: Crazy Rasputin, hanging around Nicholas's inner circle to act superior

indicators.note: hanging around is read as surrounding the round letter
crazy means the letters are deranged and rearranged

parts.note: the ring-shaped letter O sits inside Nicholas

explanation.surface: The mad monk loiters near Tsar Nicholas's close courtiers, giving himself airs.
explanation.walkthrough: Rasputin was famously influential at the court of Tsar Nicholas II, which makes the surface vivid.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave as if better than others is to adopt a haughty, pretentious manner.

clue.text: Passage from saga is learnable

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An extract from a long saga is easy to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats or shelves is a passage through them.

clue.text: Don't get me wrong number, belonging to criminal!

parts.note: of expresses belonging, as in friend of mine
a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods

explanation.surface: A misprinted phone number turns out to be a criminal's, so the caller apologises.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are apologetic phrases used to stop a remark being taken as an insult.

clue.text: Bean that gives you a bit of wind

definitions.meaning: a small pale green kidney bean
a small flute, one member of the woodwind family

explanation.surface: A joke about beans causing flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the windy effects of beans; really the second sense is a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a French haricot variety and a small fipple flute in the orchestra's wind section.

clue.text: Hoist 90 ton? That's nothing

indicators.note: hoist means heaved up and tossed about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: ninety spells out the number

explanation.surface: Lifting ninety tons is dismissed as no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: '90' must be spelt out as a word before its letters join those of TON for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of no importance is a nobody, so 'nothing' in the sense of a nobody fits.

clue.text: Subject to choice? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a pick is a choice, as in take your pick

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a matter is optional and is told only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject of discussion or study is the theme or matter being dealt with.

clue.text: Practice holding grudge at a point in the near future

definitions.text: at a point in the near future

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: to ply a trade is to practise it
to resent is to begrudge

explanation.surface: Rehearsing while nursing a grievance, until a time soon to come.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means soon, shortly, before long, which is a moment in the near future.

clue.text: Bewildered fly-half surrounded by non-drinkers

indicators.note: surrounded by means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members abstain
half of tsetse, the African fly, is tse

explanation.surface: A rugby fly-half is baffled when hemmed in by teetotallers.
explanation.walkthrough: A fly-half is a rugby position, but here it is half of TSETSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lost or all at sea is to be confused and uncertain what to do.

clue.text: Followed twisting route north-east then south, start to finish not being in gear?

indicators.note: start to finish means the opening letter is shifted to the end

parts.note: a path that winds like a serpent snaked along
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: Directions for a winding drive that ends with the car not engaged in gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to finish' moves the first S of SNAKEDNES S to the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is also clothing, so being without any gear on is to be unclothed.

clue.text: Problem child

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute or a point of concern
offspring, as in died without children

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a point of difficulty under discussion, and in law and formal usage a person's offspring.

clue.text: Cut, and cut hard

indicators.note: cut means the final letter is chopped off

parts.note: severe means harsh or hard

explanation.surface: A demand for a deep, harsh reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Cut' is the definition, the second the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever something is to slice it off or divide it completely.

clue.text: Bad name, one I try to scrap

indicators.note: scrap means break up, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone with a poor reputation resolves to get rid of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being famous for something bad gives a person an infamous reputation.

clue.text: Non-lethal weapon was tested once more during uprising

indicators.note: in a down answer an uprising reads the letters from the bottom up

parts.note: resat means sat an exam again

explanation.surface: A stun gun was trialled again amid a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: This electroshock device incapacitates rather than kills, as used by police.

clue.text: Drive metal fastening through, but don't bore

definitions.meaning: to join plates by hammering a metal pin through them
to hold someone's attention completely, to fascinate

explanation.surface: Workshop advice: hammer the fixing through rather than drilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like drilling, which fits the workshop scene; it means to tire someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a metal pin used for fastening and a verb meaning to engross or captivate.

clue.text: Innovations associated with Jon Snow?

definitions.meaning: Jon Snow, the Channel 4 News presenter, was known for colourful neckwear

explanation.surface: A question whether new ideas are linked to the newsreader Jon Snow.
explanation.walkthrough: Jon Snow presented Channel 4 News in Britain for decades, famous for his bold ties.
explanation.definitionFit: New and unusual things or ideas are fresh inventions, things that are new.

clue.text: One putting cross into box from left or right wing, perhaps?

definitions.text: One putting cross into box from left or right wing, perhaps?

parts.words: One putting cross into box from left or right wing, perhaps?
parts.note: reads like a football winger crossing into the penalty area, but describes someone marking a ballot paper for a party of the left or right

explanation.surface: A winger crosses the ball into the penalty area from either flank.
explanation.definitionFit: At an election a person marks an X on the ballot and places it in the ballot box, perhaps backing left or right.

clue.text: Really rather twee

parts.note: pretty can mean very, as in pretty good
pretty also means fairly, as in pretty tired

explanation.surface: Something is judged to be quite overly cute.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively quaint or sweet, and the doubled word describes a sugary, over-dainty prettiness.
